# Adjudication Task — Chapter 321

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃321화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“지금…… 뭐라 하였느냐?”
  6|
  7|황보엄의 목소리는 금방이라도 끊어질 듯 아슬아슬했다.
  8|
  9|그를 신선처럼 보이게 했던 새하얀 수염은 부풀어 올랐고, 나를 응시하는 한 쌍의 눈동자는 차갑게 굳어 있었다.
 10|
 11|나는 부드럽게 웃으며 대답했다.
 12|
 13|“방금 말씀드리지 않았습니까. 무슨 개수작을 부리나 와 봤다고요. 우. 연. 히.”
 14|
 15|그 순간, 황보엄의 눈에서 시퍼런 불똥이 튀었다.
 16|
 17|“갈(喝)-!”
 18|
 19|노호성과 함께 황보엄을 중심으로 막대한 기파가 뻗어 나왔다.
 20|
 21|초절정 고수가 발산한 기세에 탁자가, 아니 지면이 풍랑을 만난 선박처럼 요동치기 시작했다.
 22|
 23|구구구구궁!
 24|
 25|거센 진동과 함께 다루 내부는 난장판이 되어 버렸다. 수십 개의 다기(茶器)가 요란한 소리를 내며 박살 났고, 찻물이 사방으로 튀었다.
 26|
 27|히익, 하는 소리와 함께 구석에서 눈치만 살피던 주인장이 털썩 주저앉는다.
 28|
 29|순간적으로 소매를 들어 주화란의 얼굴에 튄 찻물을 막아 낸 내가 쯧쯧 혀를 찼다.
 30|
 31|“나이도 드실 만큼 드신 분이 남의 가게에서 행패를 부리시면 안 되죠. 다른 사람들도 있는데.”
 32|
 33|“네놈이 감히…….”
 34|
 35|황보엄에게서 느껴지는 기세가 한층 더 강해졌다.
 36|
 37|다른 누구도 아닌 종남제일검의 기세다. 그의 주위를 호위하듯 둘러싸고 있던 태을검대의 검수들마저 불에 덴 듯 화들짝 놀라며 뒷걸음질 쳤고, 주화란을 포함한 용봉표국의 인물들은 얼굴이 새하얗게 질렸다.
 38|
 39|“흐읍!”
 40|
 41|“헉!”
 42|
 43|제아무리 뛰어난 후기지수라고 해도 황보엄과는 하늘과 땅 정도의 수준 차이가 있다.
 44|
 45|화산파의 동량지재라는 백무성, 십만 방도를 보유한 개방의 후개인 궁기방도 주화란과 크게 다르지 않았다.
 46|
 47|이 자리의 모두를 포함해도 멀쩡해 보이는 이는 셋 정도에 불과하다.
 48|
 49|그중 한 명은 당연히 나고.
 50|
 51|“은인. 당과 언제 나와요?”
 52|
 53|남은 둘 중 하나는 태을무정검이고 나발이고 간에 당과만 찾는 청풍.
 54|
 55|그리고 마지막은…….
 56|
 57|“으음.”
 58|
 59|사나운 눈매의 표사, 송일섬이었다.
 60|
 61|황보엄의 기세에 작게 침음성을 흘리던 그는 나와 눈을 마주치자 눈썹을 찡그리더니 고개를 돌렸다.
 62|
 63|‘나도 너 싫어, 새꺄.’
 64|
 65|처음 봤을 때부터 지금까지, 송일섬은 여러모로 구린내를 풍기던 놈이었다.
 66|
 67|그런 내 생각이 착각인지, 사실인지 알게 되기까지는 그리 오랜 시간이 걸리지 않을 것이다.
 68|
 69|“환기를 안 해서 그런가, 공기가 어째 답답하네요.”
 70|
 71|나는 태연하게 말하며 공력을 일으켰다. 단전에 웅크리고 있던 백 년의 공력이 보이지 않는 장막처럼 탁자 사이에 드리워진다.
 72|
 73|그제야 압박감에서 벗어난 주화란이 참았던 숨을 토했다.
 74|
 75|“주 소저, 괜찮아요?”
 76|
 77|“네, 네.”
 78|
 79|숨을 헐떡이던 주화란이 내 옷소매를 꽉 움켜쥐었다.
 80|
 81|“감사해요, 진 소협. 하지만 이건…….”
 82|
 83|“그만.”
 84|
 85|그녀의 목소리는 황보엄의 한마디에 의해 가로막혔다.
 86|
 87|어느덧 신선에서 악귀로 변한 그는 살기를 담아 나를 노려보고 있었다.
 88|
 89|“어린놈의 건방이 하늘을 찌르는구나.”
 90|
 91|“제가 원래 좀 잘 찌릅니다. 창을 쓰거든요.”
 92|
 93|“네놈이 지금 무슨 짓거리를 벌이는지 알고 있느냐?”
 94|
 95|“그럼요.”
 96|
 97|나는 딱딱한 의자 등받이에 느슨하게 몸을 기대며 말을 이었다.
 98|
 99|“누군가 파 놓은 함정에 빠진 죄 없는 사람들을 구해 내는 중이죠. 물론 지나가던 중에 우연히.”
100|
101|“함정이라. 그 누군가는 필시 본문을 가리킨 말이렷다.”
102|
103|“뭐, 그 부분은 좋을 대로 생각하십시오.”
104|
105|황보엄의 눈에 서렸던 진노가 수그러들었다. 이내 그의 입가에 맺힌 것은 명백한 비웃음이었다.
106|
107|“모든 말에는 책임이 따른다는 것을 모르는 모양이군.”
108|
109|“제가 이 자리에 온 걸 보니까, 저 스스로도 잘 아는 모양인데요.”
110|
111|“아해야, 지금 네 녀석은 증명할 수 없는 헛소리로 본문을 모욕했다. 대종남파를 적으로 돌리고 싶으냐?”
112|
113|“같은 정파의 무림 동도끼리 적아를 따지니까 웃기네요. 혹시 사파세요?”
114|
115|“놈!”
116|
117|“용봉표국과의 사정은 이미 들어서 알고 있습니다. 그래서 이 자리에 온 거고요.”
118|
119|나는 탁자 위를 뒹굴고 있는 설삼을 집어 들며 말을 이었다.
120|
121|지금 내 손에 들린 이것은 분명 뛰어난 영약(靈藥)이다. 그러나 아이템 감정을 통해 본 이름은 바뀌지 않았다.
122|
123|‘백년설삼.’
124|
125|종남파가 용봉표국에 운송을 의뢰한 물건이 천년설삼인 것은 이미 알고 있다. 복용만으로도 단숨에 일 갑자의 공력을 얻게 된다는, 그야말로 천고의 영약.
126|
127|무림인들이 목숨을 걸고서라도 얻기를 원하는 귀물이니 그 가치는 부르는 게 값이라고 했다.
128|
129|‘궁기방이 물어 온 정보에 의하면 용봉표국은 이번 표행에 사활을 걸었다.’
130|
131|주화란이 바보가 아닌 이상 그런 중요한 표물을 수레에 던져두고 나 몰라라 했을 리는 없다.
132|
133|그런데 천년설삼은 어디 가고 한참 급이 떨어지는 백년설삼이 왜 여기 있는 걸까.
134|
135|‘뻔하지.’
136|
137|종남파, 혹은 황보엄 개인이 손을 썼다고밖에 볼 수 없다.
138|
139|더군다나 종남파는 지난 2년 동안 용봉표국의 몰락에 깊숙이 관여했다.
140|
141|정보력으로는 하오문과 천하제일을 다툰다는 개방의 서안 분타는 이미 모든 정황을 대부분 파악했다.
142|
143|‘마지막 종지부라는 거겠지.’
144|
145|천년설삼은 코너에 몰린 용봉표국을 쓰러트릴 마지막 일격이다.
146|
147|낚아챌 수밖에 없는 먹음직스러운 미끼를 던졌고, 그 아래에 빠져나올 수 없는 함정을 팠다. 그 결과가 지금 눈앞에 펼쳐져 있다.
148|
149|하지만…….
150|
151|“제가 살아 보니까 세상일이라는 게 그렇더라고요. 다 끝난 것처럼 보여도 예상치 못한 뭔가가 불쑥 튀어나와서 죄다 흐트러지는, 그런 거.”
152|
153|나직하게 중얼거리는 나를 황보엄이 가소롭다는 듯 바라보았다.
154|
155|“젖비린내도 가시지 않은 놈이 혓바닥만 놀리는군. 산서 촌놈이 화왕의 제자가 되었다고 보이는 것이 없느냐?”
156|
157|“아직 젊으니 걱정하지 않으셔도 됩니다. 오히려 황보 대협께서 노안을 걱정하셔야 할 것 같은데요.”
158|
159|“그 사특한 주둥이를 어떻게 찢어 주어야 할까.”
160|
161|“제 주둥이가 사특한 건 모르겠고, 종남파 특은 알고 있습니다. 정작 강자 앞에서는 한마디도 못 한다는 거. 일 년 전이었던가? 황보 대협의 사형 되시는 분께서 선행 학습 해 주고 가셨거든요.”
162|
163|아직도 똑똑히 뇌리에 남아 있다. 종남파라는 이름을 앞세워 태원진가를 압박하던 노호검객의 모습이.
164|
165|화왕 적천강의 등장에 제대로 된 말 한마디 못 하고 쫓겨나던 뒷모습까지도.
166|
167|나는 입을 꾹 다문 채 황보엄의 옆자리에 앉아 있는 혁소평을 바라보며 말을 이었다.
168|
169|“하루 전에는 복습도 했고요.”
170|
171|황보엄은 눈치가 빠른 노인네였다.
172|
173|어떻게 된 일인지 알아차린 그가 혀를 차며 중얼거렸다.
174|
175|“……벌레 같은 놈들이 본문에 득실거리는군.”
176|
177|“그래도 독충(毒蟲)보다는 해충(害蟲)이 낫지 않겠습니까. 제 관점에서는 술에 취해서 난동 피우는 게 멀쩡한 표국 하나 패가망신시키는 것보다 훨씬 모범적이라서.”
178|
179|“노부에게 독충이라? 허허, 허허허!”
180|
181|내 예상과는 달리, 이제 황보엄에게서는 어떤 동요도 느껴지지 않았다.
182|
183|그는 이미 나를 포함한 모두를 내리깔아 보고 있었다. 마치 하늘 위의 솔개가 먹잇감을 낚아챌 준비를 끝낸 것처럼.
184|
185|“아해야, 대종남파를, 그리고 노부를 적으로 돌린다는 것이 무슨 뜻인지 아느냐?”
186|
187|주름진 손이 탁자를 짚었다. 엎질러진 찻물이 천천히 솟구치더니 화살의 형태로 화하여 정확히 내 미간을 겨누었다.
188|
189|“노부가 마음만 먹는다면, 네놈은 오늘이 바로 제삿날이니라.”
190|
191|그건 당신 생각이지.
192|
193|나는 내심 그런 생각을 하며 입을 열었다.
194|
195|“글쎄요. 제 입장에서나 대협 입장에서나, 양쪽 모두에게 썩 좋은 선택은 아닌 것 같은데요.”
196|
197|“그렇기에 네놈이 지금껏 살아 있는 것이다. 오늘의 일은 노부가 후에 친히 치죄할 터. 개죽음당하기 싫다면 물러나거라. 이건 본문과 용봉표국 간의 일이니라.”
198|
199|막 대답하려는 그때, 소매를 잡아끄는 손길이 있었다.
200|
201|동시에 떨리는 여인의 목소리가 공력을 타고 내 귓가를 파고들었다.
202|
203|- 진 소협…….
204|
205|이틀 전, 티 하나 없이 맑게 반짝이던 주화란의 눈동자는 혼란스러운 감정들로 소용돌이치고 있었다.
206|
207|지금 상황에 대한 두려움과 분노. 그리고 내 등장으로 인한 안도와 걱정까지.
208|
209|그녀가 무슨 생각을 하고 있는지, 무슨 말을 하려는지 충분히 알 수 있었다.
210|
211|- 생각해 주신 것은 감사하지만…… 그의 말이 맞아요. 이건 용봉표국과 종남파의 일. 더 관여하신다면 진 소협까지 위험에 빠지게 될 거예요.
212|
213|주화란의 눈동자를 들여다보고 있자니 문득 일 년 전의 기억이 떠오른다.
214|
215|노호검객이 어처구니없는 이유로 태원진가의 봉문을 입에 담았던 그 날, 적천강이 나타나지 않았다면 어떻게 되었을까.
216|
217|‘정파(正派)? 개 같은 소리하고 자빠졌네.’
218|
219|힘 있는 자가 생각하는 올바름이란, 약자의 그것과는 다르다.
220|
221|정파 무림에 속한 모두가 악하다고 여기지는 않겠다. 하지만 동시에 모두가 선하다고 생각하지도 않는다.
222|
223|소림사에도 악한 마음을 품은 이는 있을 것이고, 흉신악살들의 소굴이라 불리는 마교에도 선한 자가 있다고 믿는다.
224|
225|정, 사, 마. 그 어느 곳에도 선과 악은 공존한다.
226|
227|‘문파가 아니라, 개인의 문제야.’
228|
229|결국 중요한 건 사람이다. 그리고 그렇게 생각하는 내 시선에 닿은 저 노인네는, 천하의 시벌놈 중 하나다.
230|
231|나는 크게 심호흡한 뒤 주화란을 향해 입을 열었다. 전음이 아닌 육성이었다.
232|
233|“주 소저.”
234|
235|“지, 진 소협?”
236|
237|“소저 말이 맞아요. 이건 종남파와 용봉표국 간의 일이고, 내가 끼어들어 봤자 오지랖에 손해만 보겠지. 아무리 태원진가가 컸어도 종남파의 이름 앞에서는 한참 부족하니까.”
238|
239|순간 놀랐던 주화란의 눈꺼풀이 파르르 떨며 내려간다.
240|
241|그녀에게서 느껴지는 짙은 체념.
242|
243|하지만 내 말은 아직 끝난 것이 아니었다.
244|
245|“사실 오면서도 그런 생각이 들더라고요. 이게 맞나, 그냥 모르는 척 지나가야 하는 게 아닌가.”
246|
247|“진 소협. 그만, 그만하셔도 돼요.”
248|
249|“아뇨.”
250|
251|나는 고개를 저으며 말을 이었다.
252|
253|“처음엔 주 소저 얼굴이 자꾸 생각나서, 단지 그것 때문인 줄만 알았어요. 그런데…….”
254|
255|시선을 돌리자 재미있다는 듯 웃고 있는 황보엄이 눈에 들어온다.
256|

I already knew that Zhongnan had commissioned the Yongbong Escort Bureau to transport Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng.

[P63]
It was a legendary elixir said to grant a full jiazi of internal energy through consumption alone.

[P64]
Murim practitioners would risk their lives to possess such a rare treasure, and its value was whatever price the seller cared to name.

[P65]
*According to the information Gung Gibang gathered, the Yongbong Escort Bureau staked its survival on this mission.*

[P66]
Unless Ju Hwaran was a complete fool, there was no way she would have thrown such precious cargo into a wagon and left it unattended.

[P67]
Then where had the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng gone? And why had it been replaced with Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng, an elixir far inferior to it?

[P68]
*It was obvious.*

[P69]
Either Zhongnan or Hwangbo Eom himself had tampered with it.

[P70]
What was more, Zhongnan had been deeply involved in the Yongbong Escort Bureau’s decline over the past two years.

[P71]
The Xi’an branch of the Beggars’ Sect, whose information network was said to rival the Lower District Sect’s for the finest under heaven, had already pieced together most of what had happened.

[P72]
*This was supposed to be the finishing blow.*

[P73]
The Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng was the final strike meant to bring down the cornered Yongbong Escort Bureau.

[P74]
They had dangled bait too tempting to resist, then dug an inescapable trap beneath it. The result was unfolding before my eyes.

[P75]
But…

[P76]
“You know, living in this world has taught me something. Even when everything looks finished, something unexpected can suddenly pop up and throw the whole thing into disarray.”

[P77]
Hwangbo Eom regarded my muttering with contempt.

[P78]
“A brat who still reeks of his mother’s milk does nothing but wag his tongue. Has becoming the Fire King’s Disciple blinded you to your place, you country bumpkin from Shanxi?”

[P79]
“I’m still young, so there’s no need to worry about my eyesight. You’re the one who should be concerned about failing vision, Great Hero Hwangbo.”

[P80]
“How should I tear apart that wicked mouth of yours?”

[P81]
“I don’t know whether my mouth is wicked, but I do know Zhongnan’s specialty. You can’t utter a word when someone stronger than you shows up. Was it a year ago? Your Senior Brother gave me an advance lesson.”

[P82]
I still remembered it clearly.

[P83]
The Roaring Fury Swordsman had invoked Zhongnan’s name to pressure the Jin Family of Taiyuan.

[P84]
I even remembered the sight of him being driven away without managing a single proper word after the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, appeared.

[P85]
I pressed my lips together and looked at Hyuk Sopyung, who sat beside Hwangbo Eom.

[P86]
“And yesterday, I had a review session.”

[P87]
Hwangbo Eom was a perceptive old man.

[P88]
Realizing what had happened, he clicked his tongue and muttered, “…Our sect is crawling with worms.”

[P89]
“Still, aren’t common pests better than venomous ones? From where I’m sitting, getting drunk and causing a scene is far more respectable than ruining a perfectly good escort bureau.”

[P90]
“You dare call this old man venomous? Hah. Hahaha!”

[P91]
Contrary to my expectations, I could no longer sense the slightest agitation from Hwangbo Eom.

[P92]
He looked down on everyone present, myself included, like a hawk high above that was ready to swoop down and seize its prey.

[P93]
“Boy, do you understand what it means to make an enemy of the Great Zhongnan Sect—and of this old man?”

[P94]
His wrinkled hand pressed against the table. The spilled tea slowly rose, took the form of an arrow, and pointed straight between my brows.

[P95]
“If this old man so desires, today will be the day you die.”

[P96]
*That’s what you think.*

[P97]
I opened my mouth.

[P98]
“Well, from either your perspective or mine, that doesn’t sound like a particularly good choice.”

[P99]
“That is why you remain alive. This old man will personally punish you for today’s offense in due time. If you do not wish to die like a dog, withdraw. This is a matter between our sect and the Yongbong Escort Bureau.”

[P100]
Just as I was about to respond, a hand tugged at my sleeve.

[P101]
At the same time, a woman’s trembling voice reached my ears, carried by internal energy.

[P102]
*—Young Hero Jin…*

[P103]
Two days ago, Ju Hwaran’s eyes had been clear and spotless. Now they swirled with conflicting emotions.

[P104]
Fear and anger at what was happening. Relief at my arrival, and worry for my safety.

[P105]
I knew exactly what she was thinking and what she wanted to say.

[P106]
*—I’m grateful for your concern, but he’s right. This is a matter between the Yongbong Escort Bureau and Zhongnan. If you involve yourself any further, you’ll be in danger too.*

[P107]
Looking into Ju Hwaran’s eyes brought back a memory from a year ago.

[P108]
The Roaring Fury Swordsman had threatened to seal the gates of the Jin Family of Taiyuan for an absurd reason. What would have happened that day if Jeok Cheongang had not appeared?

[P109]
*Orthodox faction? What a load of fucking bullshit.*

[P110]
The righteousness of the powerful was not the same as the righteousness of the weak.

[P111]
I did not believe everyone in the orthodox Murim was evil. At the same time, I did not believe they were all good.

[P112]
Even Shaolin Temple surely had people with wicked hearts, and I believed there were good people even within the Demonic Cult, that supposed den of fiends and monsters.

[P113]
Orthodox, unorthodox, demonic. Good and evil existed in all three.

[P114]
*It isn’t about the sect. It’s about the person.*

[P115]
In the end, the individual was what mattered. And the old man before me was one of the biggest fucking bastards under heaven.

[P116]
I took a deep breath, then spoke to Ju Hwaran aloud rather than using Sound Transmission.

[P117]
“Young Lady Ju.”

[P118]
“Y-Young Hero Jin?”

[P119]
“You’re right. This is between Zhongnan and the Yongbong Escort Bureau. If I stick my nose into it, all I’ll get for my trouble is a loss. No matter how much the Jin Family of Taiyuan has grown, we still fall far short of Zhongnan.”

[P120]
Ju Hwaran’s eyelids fluttered with surprise, then lowered.

[P121]
I could feel her sinking into resignation.

[P122]
But I was not finished.

[P123]
“I kept thinking the same thing on the way here. Wondering whether this was really the right choice, or whether I should pretend I knew nothing and keep walking.”

[P124]
“Young Hero Jin, you can stop. Please, that’s enough.”

[P125]
“No.”

[P126]
I shook my head.

[P127]
“At first, I thought I was doing this because your face kept coming to mind. But…”

[P128]
I turned and found Hwangbo Eom watching me with an amused smile.

[P129]
Zhongnan was one of the Nine Sects and One Gang, and Hwangbo Eom was its elder and greatest martial artist.

[P130]
His martial arts were stronger and his schemes more meticulous, but he was still the same kind of man as the Roaring Fury Swordsman.

[P131]
I stared straight at this second Roaring Fury Swordsman and opened my mouth.

[P132]
“It was fucking disgusting.”

[P133]
“……!”

[P134]
“……!”

[P135]
Even without looking around, I could feel the room stir.

[P136]
I continued with a sigh.

[P137]
“‘Upright.’ That’s why you’re called the orthodox faction. But there’s nothing upright about this, is there? If you’re going to act like this, use the *jeong* from Choco Pie instead. Why the fuck would you use the *jeong* that means ‘upright’?”[^1]

[P138]
Never once in my life had I thought of myself as a good person.

[P139]
I had become a Hunter for money, and in the Murim, I had even considered abandoning someone to save my own life.

[P140]
I was a murky gray. Nothing more, nothing less.

[P141]
Yet now, a thought suddenly occurred to me.

[P142]
“Maybe I was pretty white after all. Why else would I go this far?”

[P143]
“You insolent little—!”

[P144]
“Great Hero Hwangbo.”

[P145]
I smiled at Hwangbo Eom as he prepared to roar.

[P146]
“I told you earlier, didn’t I? Even when everything seems over, something unexpected can suddenly pop up and throw it all into disarray.”

[P147]
I slowly reached out and tapped the empty air.

[P148]
No one else could see it, but I could.

[P149]
Hwangbo Eom’s dominoes were tumbling one after another.

[P150]
“I’m not even your grandson, Great Hero Hwangbo. Why else would I spend this long talking to an eighty-year-old grandfather?”

[P151]
For an instant, Hwangbo Eom looked dumbfounded. Then his face twisted violently.

[P152]
He had sensed it too—the presences of several people rapidly approaching the teahouse.

[P153]
“You bastard. What the hell are you plotting?”

[P154]
“You’re the one who pulled a trick. I…”

[P155]
I turned my head and finished.

[P156]
“I made a plan.”

[P157]
At that moment, the teahouse doors opened and more than a dozen people poured inside.

[P158]
First came five beggars carrying mountains of bamboo slips in their arms. They were the Xi’an Branch Leader of the Beggars’ Sect and his subordinates.

[P159]
At the head of the other group stood a woman I knew well.

[P160]
“Congratulations on your promotion. It’s been a while.”

[P161]
“Oh, my Young Master. A congratulatory greeting after an entire year? How prompt of you.”

[P162]
Wolhwa, Branch Leader of the Lower District Sect’s Shaanxi branch, playfully arched one pretty eyebrow.

[P163]
[^1]: This is a pun on *jeong*, the Korean word associated with affection in Choco Pie’s famous slogan, contrasted with the *jeong* in “orthodox,” which means upright or righteous.
```

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 321

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃321화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“지금…… 뭐라 하였느냐?”
  6|
  7|황보엄의 목소리는 금방이라도 끊어질 듯 아슬아슬했다.
  8|
  9|그를 신선처럼 보이게 했던 새하얀 수염은 부풀어 올랐고, 나를 응시하는 한 쌍의 눈동자는 차갑게 굳어 있었다.
 10|
 11|나는 부드럽게 웃으며 대답했다.
 12|
 13|“방금 말씀드리지 않았습니까. 무슨 개수작을 부리나 와 봤다고요. 우. 연. 히.”
 14|
 15|그 순간, 황보엄의 눈에서 시퍼런 불똥이 튀었다.
 16|
 17|“갈(喝)-!”
 18|
 19|노호성과 함께 황보엄을 중심으로 막대한 기파가 뻗어 나왔다.
 20|
 21|초절정 고수가 발산한 기세에 탁자가, 아니 지면이 풍랑을 만난 선박처럼 요동치기 시작했다.
 22|
 23|구구구구궁!
 24|
 25|거센 진동과 함께 다루 내부는 난장판이 되어 버렸다. 수십 개의 다기(茶器)가 요란한 소리를 내며 박살 났고, 찻물이 사방으로 튀었다.
 26|
 27|히익, 하는 소리와 함께 구석에서 눈치만 살피던 주인장이 털썩 주저앉는다.
 28|
 29|순간적으로 소매를 들어 주화란의 얼굴에 튄 찻물을 막아 낸 내가 쯧쯧 혀를 찼다.
 30|
 31|“나이도 드실 만큼 드신 분이 남의 가게에서 행패를 부리시면 안 되죠. 다른 사람들도 있는데.”
 32|
 33|“네놈이 감히…….”
 34|
 35|황보엄에게서 느껴지는 기세가 한층 더 강해졌다.
 36|
 37|다른 누구도 아닌 종남제일검의 기세다. 그의 주위를 호위하듯 둘러싸고 있던 태을검대의 검수들마저 불에 덴 듯 화들짝 놀라며 뒷걸음질 쳤고, 주화란을 포함한 용봉표국의 인물들은 얼굴이 새하얗게 질렸다.
 38|
 39|“흐읍!”
 40|
 41|“헉!”
 42|
 43|제아무리 뛰어난 후기지수라고 해도 황보엄과는 하늘과 땅 정도의 수준 차이가 있다.
 44|
 45|화산파의 동량지재라는 백무성, 십만 방도를 보유한 개방의 후개인 궁기방도 주화란과 크게 다르지 않았다.
 46|
 47|이 자리의 모두를 포함해도 멀쩡해 보이는 이는 셋 정도에 불과하다.
 48|
 49|그중 한 명은 당연히 나고.
 50|
 51|“은인. 당과 언제 나와요?”
 52|
 53|남은 둘 중 하나는 태을무정검이고 나발이고 간에 당과만 찾는 청풍.
 54|
 55|그리고 마지막은…….
 56|
 57|“으음.”
 58|
 59|사나운 눈매의 표사, 송일섬이었다.
 60|
 61|황보엄의 기세에 작게 침음성을 흘리던 그는 나와 눈을 마주치자 눈썹을 찡그리더니 고개를 돌렸다.
 62|
 63|‘나도 너 싫어, 새꺄.’
 64|
 65|처음 봤을 때부터 지금까지, 송일섬은 여러모로 구린내를 풍기던 놈이었다.
 66|
 67|그런 내 생각이 착각인지, 사실인지 알게 되기까지는 그리 오랜 시간이 걸리지 않을 것이다.
 68|
 69|“환기를 안 해서 그런가, 공기가 어째 답답하네요.”
 70|
 71|나는 태연하게 말하며 공력을 일으켰다. 단전에 웅크리고 있던 백 년의 공력이 보이지 않는 장막처럼 탁자 사이에 드리워진다.
 72|
 73|그제야 압박감에서 벗어난 주화란이 참았던 숨을 토했다.
 74|
 75|“주 소저, 괜찮아요?”
 76|
 77|“네, 네.”
 78|
 79|숨을 헐떡이던 주화란이 내 옷소매를 꽉 움켜쥐었다.
 80|
 81|“감사해요, 진 소협. 하지만 이건…….”
 82|
 83|“그만.”
 84|
 85|그녀의 목소리는 황보엄의 한마디에 의해 가로막혔다.
 86|
 87|어느덧 신선에서 악귀로 변한 그는 살기를 담아 나를 노려보고 있었다.
 88|
 89|“어린놈의 건방이 하늘을 찌르는구나.”
 90|
 91|“제가 원래 좀 잘 찌릅니다. 창을 쓰거든요.”
 92|
 93|“네놈이 지금 무슨 짓거리를 벌이는지 알고 있느냐?”
 94|
 95|“그럼요.”
 96|
 97|나는 딱딱한 의자 등받이에 느슨하게 몸을 기대며 말을 이었다.
 98|
 99|“누군가 파 놓은 함정에 빠진 죄 없는 사람들을 구해 내는 중이죠. 물론 지나가던 중에 우연히.”
100|
101|“함정이라. 그 누군가는 필시 본문을 가리킨 말이렷다.”
102|
103|“뭐, 그 부분은 좋을 대로 생각하십시오.”
104|
105|황보엄의 눈에 서렸던 진노가 수그러들었다. 이내 그의 입가에 맺힌 것은 명백한 비웃음이었다.
106|
107|“모든 말에는 책임이 따른다는 것을 모르는 모양이군.”
108|
109|“제가 이 자리에 온 걸 보니까, 저 스스로도 잘 아는 모양인데요.”
110|
111|“아해야, 지금 네 녀석은 증명할 수 없는 헛소리로 본문을 모욕했다. 대종남파를 적으로 돌리고 싶으냐?”
112|
113|“같은 정파의 무림 동도끼리 적아를 따지니까 웃기네요. 혹시 사파세요?”
114|
115|“놈!”
116|
117|“용봉표국과의 사정은 이미 들어서 알고 있습니다. 그래서 이 자리에 온 거고요.”
118|
119|나는 탁자 위를 뒹굴고 있는 설삼을 집어 들며 말을 이었다.
120|
121|지금 내 손에 들린 이것은 분명 뛰어난 영약(靈藥)이다. 그러나 아이템 감정을 통해 본 이름은 바뀌지 않았다.
122|
123|‘백년설삼.’
124|
125|종남파가 용봉표국에 운송을 의뢰한 물건이 천년설삼인 것은 이미 알고 있다. 복용만으로도 단숨에 일 갑자의 공력을 얻게 된다는, 그야말로 천고의 영약.
126|
127|무림인들이 목숨을 걸고서라도 얻기를 원하는 귀물이니 그 가치는 부르는 게 값이라고 했다.
128|
129|‘궁기방이 물어 온 정보에 의하면 용봉표국은 이번 표행에 사활을 걸었다.’
130|
131|주화란이 바보가 아닌 이상 그런 중요한 표물을 수레에 던져두고 나 몰라라 했을 리는 없다.
132|
133|그런데 천년설삼은 어디 가고 한참 급이 떨어지는 백년설삼이 왜 여기 있는 걸까.
134|
135|‘뻔하지.’
136|
137|종남파, 혹은 황보엄 개인이 손을 썼다고밖에 볼 수 없다.
138|
139|더군다나 종남파는 지난 2년 동안 용봉표국의 몰락에 깊숙이 관여했다.
140|
141|정보력으로는 하오문과 천하제일을 다툰다는 개방의 서안 분타는 이미 모든 정황을 대부분 파악했다.
142|
143|‘마지막 종지부라는 거겠지.’
144|
145|천년설삼은 코너에 몰린 용봉표국을 쓰러트릴 마지막 일격이다.
146|
147|낚아챌 수밖에 없는 먹음직스러운 미끼를 던졌고, 그 아래에 빠져나올 수 없는 함정을 팠다. 그 결과가 지금 눈앞에 펼쳐져 있다.
148|
149|하지만…….
150|
151|“제가 살아 보니까 세상일이라는 게 그렇더라고요. 다 끝난 것처럼 보여도 예상치 못한 뭔가가 불쑥 튀어나와서 죄다 흐트러지는, 그런 거.”
152|
153|나직하게 중얼거리는 나를 황보엄이 가소롭다는 듯 바라보았다.
154|
155|“젖비린내도 가시지 않은 놈이 혓바닥만 놀리는군. 산서 촌놈이 화왕의 제자가 되었다고 보이는 것이 없느냐?”
156|
157|“아직 젊으니 걱정하지 않으셔도 됩니다. 오히려 황보 대협께서 노안을 걱정하셔야 할 것 같은데요.”
158|
159|“그 사특한 주둥이를 어떻게 찢어 주어야 할까.”
160|
161|“제 주둥이가 사특한 건 모르겠고, 종남파 특은 알고 있습니다. 정작 강자 앞에서는 한마디도 못 한다는 거. 일 년 전이었던가? 황보 대협의 사형 되시는 분께서 선행 학습 해 주고 가셨거든요.”
162|
163|아직도 똑똑히 뇌리에 남아 있다. 종남파라는 이름을 앞세워 태원진가를 압박하던 노호검객의 모습이.
164|
165|화왕 적천강의 등장에 제대로 된 말 한마디 못 하고 쫓겨나던 뒷모습까지도.
166|
167|나는 입을 꾹 다문 채 황보엄의 옆자리에 앉아 있는 혁소평을 바라보며 말을 이었다.
168|
169|“하루 전에는 복습도 했고요.”
170|
171|황보엄은 눈치가 빠른 노인네였다.
172|
173|어떻게 된 일인지 알아차린 그가 혀를 차며 중얼거렸다.
174|
175|“……벌레 같은 놈들이 본문에 득실거리는군.”
176|
177|“그래도 독충(毒蟲)보다는 해충(害蟲)이 낫지 않겠습니까. 제 관점에서는 술에 취해서 난동 피우는 게 멀쩡한 표국 하나 패가망신시키는 것보다 훨씬 모범적이라서.”
178|
179|“노부에게 독충이라? 허허, 허허허!”
180|
181|내 예상과는 달리, 이제 황보엄에게서는 어떤 동요도 느껴지지 않았다.
182|
183|그는 이미 나를 포함한 모두를 내리깔아 보고 있었다. 마치 하늘 위의 솔개가 먹잇감을 낚아챌 준비를 끝낸 것처럼.
184|
185|“아해야, 대종남파를, 그리고 노부를 적으로 돌린다는 것이 무슨 뜻인지 아느냐?”
186|
187|주름진 손이 탁자를 짚었다. 엎질러진 찻물이 천천히 솟구치더니 화살의 형태로 화하여 정확히 내 미간을 겨누었다.
188|
189|“노부가 마음만 먹는다면, 네놈은 오늘이 바로 제삿날이니라.”
190|
191|그건 당신 생각이지.
192|
193|나는 내심 그런 생각을 하며 입을 열었다.
194|
195|“글쎄요. 제 입장에서나 대협 입장에서나, 양쪽 모두에게 썩 좋은 선택은 아닌 것 같은데요.”
196|
197|“그렇기에 네놈이 지금껏 살아 있는 것이다. 오늘의 일은 노부가 후에 친히 치죄할 터. 개죽음당하기 싫다면 물러나거라. 이건 본문과 용봉표국 간의 일이니라.”
198|
199|막 대답하려는 그때, 소매를 잡아끄는 손길이 있었다.
200|
201|동시에 떨리는 여인의 목소리가 공력을 타고 내 귓가를 파고들었다.
202|
203|- 진 소협…….
204|
205|이틀 전, 티 하나 없이 맑게 반짝이던 주화란의 눈동자는 혼란스러운 감정들로 소용돌이치고 있었다.
206|
207|지금 상황에 대한 두려움과 분노. 그리고 내 등장으로 인한 안도와 걱정까지.
208|

[P6]
“Didn’t I just tell you? I came to see what kind of dirty trick you were pulling. By. Chance.”

[P7]
Blue sparks flew from Hwangbo Eom’s eyes.

[P8]
“Hah!”

[P9]
With his thunderous roar, an immense wave of qi erupted from him.

[P10]
The aura of a Supreme Peak master made the table—or rather, the ground itself—pitch like a ship caught in a storm.

[P11]
*Rumble!*

[P12]
The violent tremors threw the entire teahouse into chaos. Dozens of pieces of teaware shattered with a deafening crash, spraying tea in every direction.

[P13]
The proprietor, who had been nervously watching from a corner, let out a shriek and collapsed to the floor.

[P14]
I instantly raised my sleeve to shield Ju Hwaran’s face from the flying tea, then clicked my tongue.

[P15]
“Someone your age shouldn’t be causing a scene in another person’s shop. Not with other people around.”

[P16]
“How dare you…”

[P17]
The pressure radiating from Hwangbo Eom intensified.

[P18]
This was the aura of none other than The First Sword of Zhongnan. Even the swordsmen of the Taeeul Sword Unit arrayed around him like guards flinched as though burned and stumbled backward. The members of the Yongbong Escort Bureau, Ju Hwaran included, went deathly pale.

[P19]
“Hngh!”

[P20]
“Gasp!”

[P21]
No matter how talented a young prodigy might be, the gulf between them and Hwangbo Eom was as vast as the distance between heaven and earth.

[P22]
Baek Museong, known as a pillar of Huashan, and Gung Gibang, Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect and its hundred thousand members, fared little better than Ju Hwaran.

[P23]
Of everyone present, only three people appeared unaffected.

[P24]
One was me, of course.

[P25]
“Benefactor, when are the candied sweets coming?”

[P26]
Another was Cheongpung, who cared only about his candied sweets, to hell with the Taeeul Merciless Sword or anything else.

[P27]
And the last was…

[P28]
“Hmm.”

[P29]
Song Ilseom, the fierce-eyed escort.

[P30]
He gave a quiet grunt under the weight of Hwangbo Eom’s aura. When our eyes met, he frowned and turned away.

[P31]
*I don’t like you either, asshole.*

[P32]
From the moment I first saw him, Song Ilseom had stunk of something suspicious in more ways than one.

[P33]
It would not be long before I learned whether that was only my imagination.

[P34]
“Maybe it’s because no one opened a window, but the air feels awfully stuffy.”

[P35]
I spoke calmly and drew up my internal energy. The hundred years of internal energy coiled within my dantian spread between the tables like an invisible curtain.

[P36]
Freed from the crushing pressure, Ju Hwaran finally released the breath she had been holding.

[P37]
“Young Lady Ju, are you all right?”

[P38]
“Y-Yes.”

[P39]
Still gasping, Ju Hwaran clutched my sleeve.

[P40]
“Thank you, Young Hero Jin. But this…”

[P41]
“Enough.”

[P42]
A single word from Hwangbo Eom cut her off.

[P43]
The immortal had transformed into a Fiend. He glared at me, his gaze brimming with killing intent.

[P44]
“The arrogance of a young whelp like you pierces the heavens.”

[P45]
“I’ve always been good at piercing things. I use a spear.”

[P46]
“Do you even understand what you’re doing?”

[P47]
“Of course.”

[P48]
I leaned back lazily against the hard wooden chair.

[P49]
“I’m rescuing innocent people who fell into a trap someone laid for them. Purely because I happened to be passing by, of course.”

[P50]
“A trap. I presume that ‘someone’ refers to our sect.”

[P51]
“Well, you’re free to think whatever you like.”

[P52]
The fury in Hwangbo Eom’s eyes subsided. In its place, an unmistakable sneer spread across his lips.

[P53]
“You seem unaware that a man must answer for his words.”

[P54]
“Judging by the fact that I came here, I’d say I’m well aware of that.”

[P55]
“Boy, you have insulted the Great Zhongnan Sect with baseless accusations you cannot prove. Do you wish to make us your enemy?”

[P56]
“It’s funny hearing fellow members of the orthodox faction divide everyone into friends and enemies. Are you sure you’re not unorthodox?”

[P57]
“You insolent whelp!”

[P58]
“I already heard what happened between the Yongbong Escort Bureau and your sect. That’s why I came.”

[P59]
I picked up the snow ginseng rolling across the table.

[P60]
What I held was undoubtedly a valuable elixir. Yet the name shown by Item Appraisal remained unchanged.

[P61]
*Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng.*

[P62]
I already knew that Zhongnan had commissioned the Yongbong Escort Bureau to transport Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng.

[P63]
It was a legendary elixir said to grant a full jiazi of internal energy through consumption alone.

[P64]
Murim practitioners would risk their lives to possess such a rare treasure, and its value was whatever price the seller cared to name.

[P65]
*According to the information Gung Gibang gathered, the Yongbong Escort Bureau staked its survival on this mission.*

[P66]
Unless Ju Hwaran was a complete fool, there was no way she would have thrown such precious cargo into a wagon and left it unattended.

[P67]
Then where had the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng gone? And why had it been replaced with Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng, an elixir far inferior to it?

[P68]
*It was obvious.*

[P69]
Either Zhongnan or Hwangbo Eom himself had tampered with it.

[P70]
What was more, Zhongnan had been deeply involved in the Yongbong Escort Bureau’s decline over the past two years.

[P71]
The Xi’an branch of the Beggars’ Sect, whose information network was said to rival the Lower District Sect’s for the finest under heaven, had already pieced together most of what had happened.

[P72]
*This was supposed to be the finishing blow.*

[P73]
The Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng was the final strike meant to bring down the cornered Yongbong Escort Bureau.

[P74]
They had dangled bait too tempting to resist, then dug an inescapable trap beneath it. The result was unfolding before my eyes.

[P75]
But…

[P76]
“You know, living in this world has taught me something. Even when everything looks finished, something unexpected can suddenly pop up and throw the whole thing into disarray.”

[P77]
Hwangbo Eom regarded my muttering with contempt.

[P78]
“A brat who still reeks of his mother’s milk does nothing but wag his tongue. Has becoming the Fire King’s Disciple blinded you to your place, you country bumpkin from Shanxi?”

[P79]
“I’m still young, so there’s no need to worry about my eyesight. You’re the one who should be concerned about failing vision, Great Hero Hwangbo.”

[P80]
“How should I tear apart that wicked mouth of yours?”

[P81]
“I don’t know whether my mouth is wicked, but I do know Zhongnan’s specialty. You can’t utter a word when someone stronger than you shows up. Was it a year ago? Your Senior Brother gave me an advance lesson.”

[P82]
I still remembered it clearly.

[P83]
The Roaring Fury Swordsman had invoked Zhongnan’s name to pressure the Jin Family of Taiyuan.

[P84]
I even remembered the sight of him being driven away without managing a single proper word after the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, appeared.

[P85]
I pressed my lips together and looked at Hyuk Sopyung, who sat beside Hwangbo Eom.

[P86]
“And yesterday, I had a review session.”

[P87]
Hwangbo Eom was a perceptive old man.

[P88]
Realizing what had happened, he clicked his tongue and muttered, “…Our sect is crawling with worms.”

[P89]
“Still, aren’t common pests better than venomous ones? From where I’m sitting, getting drunk and causing a scene is far more respectable than ruining a perfectly good escort bureau.”

[P90]
“You dare call this old man venomous? Hah. Hahaha!”

[P91]
Contrary to my expectations, I could no longer sense the slightest agitation from Hwangbo Eom.

[P92]
He looked down on everyone present, myself included, like a hawk high above that was ready to swoop down and seize its prey.

[P93]
“Boy, do you understand what it means to make an enemy of the Great Zhongnan Sect—and of this old man?”

[P94]
His wrinkled hand pressed against the table. The spilled tea slowly rose, took the form of an arrow, and pointed straight between my brows.

[P95]
“If this old man so desires, today will be the day you die.”

[P96]
*That’s what you think.*

[P97]
I opened my mouth.

[P98]
“Well, from either your perspective or mine, that doesn’t sound like a particularly good choice.”

[P99]
“That is why you remain alive. This old man will personally punish you for today’s offense in due time. If you do not wish to die like a dog, withdraw. This is a matter between our sect and the Yongbong Escort Bureau.”

[P100]
Just as I was about to respond, a hand tugged at my sleeve.

[P101]
At the same time, a woman’s trembling voice reached my ears, carried by internal energy.

[P102]
*—Young Hero Jin…*

[P103]
Two days ago, Ju Hwaran’s eyes had been clear and spotless. Now they swirled with conflicting emotions.

[P104]
Fear and anger at what was happening. Relief at my arrival, and worry for my safety.

[P105]
I knew exactly what she was thinking and what she wanted to say.

[P106]
*—I’m grateful for your concern, but he’s right. This is a matter between the Yongbong Escort Bureau and Zhongnan. If you involve yourself any further, you’ll be in danger too.*

[P107]
Looking into Ju Hwaran’s eyes brought back a memory from a year ago.

[P108]
The Roaring Fury Swordsman had threatened to seal the gates of the Jin Family of Taiyuan for an absurd reason. What would have happened that day if Jeok Cheongang had not appeared?

[P109]
*Orthodox faction? What a load of fucking bullshit.*

[P110]
The righteousness of the powerful was not the same as the righteousness of the weak.

[P111]
I did not believe everyone in the orthodox Murim was evil. At the same time, I did not believe they were all good.

[P112]
Even Shaolin Temple surely had people with wicked hearts, and I believed there were good people even within the Demonic Cult, that supposed den of fiends and monsters.

[P113]
Orthodox, unorthodox, demonic. Good and evil existed in all three.

[P114]
*It isn’t about the sect. It’s about the person.*

[P115]
In the end, the individual was what mattered. And the old man before me was one of the biggest fucking bastards under heaven.

[P116]
I took a deep breath, then spoke to Ju Hwaran aloud rather than using Sound Transmission.

[P117]
“Young Lady Ju.”

[P118]
“Y-Young Hero Jin?”

[P119]
“You’re right. This is between Zhongnan and the Yongbong Escort Bureau. If I stick my nose into it, all I’ll get for my trouble is a loss. No matter how much the Jin Family of Taiyuan has grown, we still fall far short of Zhongnan.”

[P120]
Ju Hwaran’s eyelids fluttered with surprise, then lowered.

[P121]
I could feel her sinking into resignation.

[P122]
But I was not finished.

[P123]
“I kept thinking the same thing on the way here. Wondering whether this was really the right choice, or whether I should pretend I knew nothing and keep walking.”

[P124]
“Young Hero Jin, you can stop. Please, that’s enough.”

[P125]
“No.”

[P126]
I shook my head.

[P127]
“At first, I thought I was doing this because your face kept coming to mind. But…”

[P128]
I turned and found Hwangbo Eom watching me with an amused smile.

[P129]
Zhongnan was one of the Nine Sects and One Gang, and Hwangbo Eom was its elder and greatest martial artist.

[P130]
His martial arts were stronger and his schemes more meticulous, but he was still the same kind of man as the Roaring Fury Swordsman.

[P131]
I stared straight at this second Roaring Fury Swordsman and opened my mouth.

[P132]
“It was fucking disgusting.”

[P133]
“……!”

[P134]
“……!”

[P135]
Even without looking around, I could feel the room stir.

[P136]
I continued with a sigh.

[P137]
“‘Upright.’ That’s why you’re called the orthodox faction. But there’s nothing upright about this, is there? If you’re going to act like this, use the *jeong* from Choco Pie instead. Why the fuck would you use the *jeong* that means ‘upright’?”[^1]

[P138]
Never once in my life had I thought of myself as a good person.

[P139]
I had become a Hunter for money, and in the Murim, I had even considered abandoning someone to save my own life.

[P140]
I was a murky gray. Nothing more, nothing less.

[P141]
Yet now, a thought suddenly occurred to me.

[P142]
“Maybe I was pretty white after all. Why else would I go this far?”

[P143]
“You insolent little—!”

[P144]
“Great Hero Hwangbo.”

[P145]
I smiled at Hwangbo Eom as he prepared to roar.

[P146]
“I told you earlier, didn’t I? Even when everything seems over, something unexpected can suddenly pop up and throw it all into disarray.”

[P147]
I slowly reached out and tapped the empty air.

[P148]
No one else could see it, but I could.

[P149]
Hwangbo Eom’s dominoes were tumbling one after another.

[P150]
“I’m not even your grandson, Great Hero Hwangbo. Why else would I spend this long talking to an eighty-year-old grandfather?”

[P151]
For an instant, Hwangbo Eom looked dumbfounded. Then his face twisted violently.

[P152]
He had sensed it too—the presences of several people rapidly approaching the teahouse.

[P153]
“You bastard. What the hell are you plotting?”

[P154]
“You’re the one who pulled a trick. I…”

[P155]
I turned my head and finished.

[P156]
“I made a plan.”

[P157]
At that moment, the teahouse doors opened and more than a dozen people poured inside.

[P158]
First came five beggars carrying mountains of bamboo slips in their arms. They were the Xi’an Branch Leader of the Beggars’ Sect and his subordinates.

[P159]
At the head of the other group stood a woman I knew well.

[P160]
“Congratulations on your promotion. It’s been a while.”

[P161]
“Oh, my Young Master. A congratulatory greeting after an entire year? How prompt of you.”

[P162]
Wolhwa, Branch Leader of the Lower District Sect’s Shaanxi branch, playfully arched one pretty eyebrow.

[P163]
[^1]: This is a pun on *jeong*, the Korean word associated with affection in Choco Pie’s famous slogan, contrasted with the *jeong* in “orthodox,” which means upright or righteous.

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.
